questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT gives examples of growth measured in different ways. According to it, cells of a watermelon may increase in size by up to:

options.text: 3,500 times
17,500 times
35 times

solution.concept: Measurement of growth by increase in cell size
solution.explanation: Growth can be measured as an increase in cell number (a maize root apical meristem gives more than 17,500 new cells per hour) or as an increase in cell size: cells of a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.
steps: Growth parameter for watermelon cells: increase in cell size
solution.why_others_wrong: 17,500 is the maize root apical meristem figure (cells per hour), not a size increase; 3,500 and 35 are invented scalings of the NCERT figure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: plant growth is measurable
solution.final_answer: Option B: 3,50,000 times

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Kinetin, the first cytokinin to be discovered, is chemically:

options.text: Indole-3-butyric acid
2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid
Naphthalene acetic acid
N6-furfurylamino purine

solution.explanation: Skoog and Miller crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting substance and named it kinetin; NCERT describes cytokinins as adenine derivatives, kinetin being N6-furfurylamino purine. IBA, 2,4-D and NAA are auxins.
solution.why_others_wrong: Indole-3-butyric acid is a natural auxin; 2,4-D and NAA are synthetic auxins.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects - cytokinins
solution.final_answer: Option D: N6-furfurylamino purine

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, development of a mature plant from a zygote is the sum of which two processes?

options.text: Dedifferentiation and redifferentiation
Cell division and senescence
Growth and differentiation
Germination and flowering

solution.explanation: NCERT opens the chapter by stating that development is the sum of two processes, growth and differentiation; the development of a mature plant from a zygote follows a precise and highly ordered succession of events.
solution.why_others_wrong: Dedifferentiation and redifferentiation are special events within development; cell division, senescence, germination and flowering are individual events, not the two component processes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option C: Growth and differentiation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following auxins has been isolated from plants (a natural auxin)?

options.text: Indole-3-butyric acid (IBA)
Naphthalene acetic acid (NAA)
2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D)
Gibberellic acid (GA₃)

solution.explanation: NCERT: IAA and indole butyric acid (IBA) have been isolated from plants, whereas NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) are synthetic auxins. GA₃ is a gibberellin, not an auxin.
solution.why_others_wrong: NAA and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins; GA₃ is a gibberellin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: physiological effects - auxins

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin observed that coleoptiles of canary grass grew towards a unilateral source of light. After a series of experiments, they concluded that:

options.text: The base of the coleoptile perceived the light and pushed the tip towards it
A gas released from the coleoptile tip hastened the bending, as ethylene does
Auxin could be isolated from the coleoptile tips and applied to cause bending
The tip of the coleoptile was the site of a transmissible influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile

solution.concept: Discovery of auxin: the Darwins' experiments
solution.explanation: The Darwins found that canary grass coleoptiles responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light (phototropism) and concluded that the tip was the site of a transmissible influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile. Auxin itself was later isolated by F.W. Went from tips of oat coleoptiles.
steps: Conclusion: tip = site of a transmissible influence
Isolation of auxin came later (Went, oat coleoptiles)
solution.why_others_wrong: The base does not perceive the stimulus in this account; the gas (ethylene) story belongs to Cousins and ripening; isolating auxin was Went's later work, not the Darwins' conclusion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: the discovery of plant growth regulators
solution.final_answer: Option D: The tip of the coleoptile was the site of a transmissible influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a root, starting at the apex and moving away from it (proximally), the phases of growth are met in the order:

options.text: Phase of elongation → meristematic phase → phase of maturation
Meristematic phase → phase of elongation → phase of maturation
Phase of maturation → phase of elongation → meristematic phase
Meristematic phase → phase of maturation → phase of elongation

solution.concept: Location of the phases of growth along the axis
solution.explanation: The constantly dividing cells at the root apex are in the meristematic phase. The cells just next to it, away from the tip, are in the phase of elongation. Further away, proximal to the elongation zone, the axis is undergoing the phase of maturation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other order places a phase out of its position relative to the apex; maturation is the farthest from the tip.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: phases of growth
solution.final_answer: Option B: Meristematic phase → phase of elongation → phase of maturation

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Gibberellins promote bolting in beet, cabbages and many other plants with a rosette habit.
Reason (R): Gibberellins promote internode elongation just prior to flowering.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the action of plant growth regulators (PGRs) are correct?

(a) The roles of PGRs in a given event can be complementary or antagonistic.
(b) PGRs may act individualistically or synergistically.
(c) Dormancy in seeds and buds, abscission, senescence and apical dominance are events in which more than one PGR interacts to affect the event.
(d) Extrinsic factors such as light and temperature never act on plant growth through PGRs.
(e) Each physiological event in a plant is controlled by a single PGR acting alone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(c), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: PGRs are one kind of intrinsic control; along with genomic control and extrinsic factors they regulate growth and development. Their roles can be complementary or antagonistic, individualistic or synergistic, and several events (seed/bud dormancy, abscission, senescence, apical dominance) are influenced by more than one PGR. Many extrinsic factors such as temperature and light control plant growth and development via PGRs.
steps: (d): false, light and temperature act via PGRs
(e): false, many events involve more than one PGR
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D each include (d) or (e), which contradict the NCERT account.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: interaction of PGRs
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (symbol in W₁ = W₀e^(rt)) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. W₁
B. W₀
C. t
D. e

List-II:
I. Base of natural logarithms
II. Time of growth
III. Final size (weight, height, number, etc.)
IV. Initial size, at the beginning of the period

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps the final and initial sizes; option B swaps time and e; option C confuses W₁ with time.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: growth rates
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the measurement and rates of plant growth are correct?

(a) Growth can be measured by a variety of parameters, such as fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number.
(b) In geometric growth, the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and thereafter it increases rapidly at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase).
(c) In arithmetic growth, both daughter cells of every mitotic division retain the ability to divide.
(d) With a limited nutrient supply, exponential growth can continue indefinitely.
(e) Relative growth rate is the growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, for example per unit initial parameter.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(a), (b) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (c) and (d) only

solution.concept: Growth parameters, lag and log phases, arithmetic growth and RGR
solution.explanation: NCERT lists fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number as growth parameters. In geometric growth the initial lag phase is slow and is followed by the log phase; with limited nutrients growth slows and a stationary phase follows, so exponential growth cannot go on indefinitely. In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. Relative growth rate is growth per unit time on a common basis, such as per unit initial parameter.
steps: (c): false, only one daughter cell keeps dividing
(d): false, limited nutrients lead to a stationary phase
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A includes (c), option C includes (d), and option D includes both (c) and (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: growth rates
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The discovery of each of the five major groups of plant growth regulators has been accidental.
Statement II: E. Kurosawa observed the symptoms of 'bakanae' disease in uninfected rice seedlings only when they were inoculated with the living fungus Gibberella fujikuroi.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that the discovery of each of the five major groups of PGRs was accidental, so Statement I is true. Kurosawa reported the appearance of bakanae symptoms in uninfected rice seedlings when they were treated with sterile filtrates of the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi; the active substance was later identified as gibberellic acid. The living fungus was not needed, so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, sterile filtrates of the fungus produced the symptoms
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: the discovery of plant growth regulators
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a woody dicot stem, which of the following is an example of redifferentiation?

options.text: Cells cut off by the interfascicular cambium that lose the capacity to divide and mature into secondary phloem cells
Formation of the interfascicular cambium from fully differentiated medullary ray parenchyma cells
Formation of the cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells
Maturation of cells derived from the root apical meristem into tracheary elements

solution.explanation: Cells from the root and shoot apical meristems and the cambium that mature to perform specific functions undergo differentiation. Fully differentiated cells regaining the capacity to divide (interfascicular cambium, cork cambium) show dedifferentiation. Cells produced by such dedifferentiated meristems that again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions are redifferentiated, e.g. secondary phloem formed from the interfascicular cambium.
steps: Interfascicular and cork cambium formation: dedifferentiation
Tracheary elements from apical meristem derivatives: differentiation
Secondary tissues formed by a dedifferentiated meristem: redifferentiation
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B and C describe dedifferentiation; option D describes differentiation of cells from a primary (apical) meristem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Cells cut off by the interfascicular cambium that lose the capacity to divide and mature into secondary phloem cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the conditions for plant growth are correct?

(a) Oxygen helps in releasing the metabolic energy essential for growth activities.
(b) Nutrients (macro and micro essential elements) are required for the synthesis of protoplasm and act as a source of energy.
(c) Environmental signals such as light and gravity also affect certain phases or stages of growth.
(d) Once a seed has germinated, the growth of the plant no longer depends on water.
(e) Light is the only environmental signal that influences plant growth.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (c) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.explanation: NCERT lists water, oxygen and nutrients as very essential for growth. Cell enlargement needs water and turgidity throughout life, so growth never becomes independent of water. Oxygen releases metabolic energy for growth; nutrients are needed for protoplasm synthesis and as a source of energy. Each plant has an optimum temperature range, and environmental signals such as light and gravity also affect certain phases of growth, so light is not the only signal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A includes (d), option B includes (e), and option C includes both.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth: conditions for growth
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical stamen has two parts, the filament and the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to:

options.text: The stigma of the same flower
The ovary wall
The thalamus or the petal of the flower
The connective of the anther only

solution.explanation: The stamen consists of a long, slender stalk called the filament and a terminal, generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower.
steps: Filament's proximal end: thalamus or petal
solution.why_others_wrong: The stigma and ovary wall belong to the pistil; the connective joins the anther lobes at the distal end of the filament, not its proximal end.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', flower: stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option C: The thalamus or the petal of the flower

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The egg apparatus of a typical angiosperm embryo sac consists of:

options.text: Three antipodal cells
Two synergids and one egg cell
One egg cell and two polar nuclei
Two synergids and two polar nuclei

solution.explanation: Six of the eight nuclei of the embryo sac are surrounded by cell walls. Three cells at the micropylar end are grouped together as the egg apparatus, which consists of two synergids and one egg cell. Three cells at the chalazal end are the antipodals, and the two polar nuclei lie in the large central cell.
steps: Micropylar end: 2 synergids + 1 egg = egg apparatus
Centre: central cell with 2 polar nuclei
solution.why_others_wrong: Antipodals are at the chalazal end; the polar nuclei lie in the central cell, not in the egg apparatus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac: female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option B: Two synergids and one egg cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following aquatic plants is pollinated by water?

options.text: Water hyacinth
Water lily
Maize
Hydrilla

solution.explanation: Pollination by water is quite rare and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocots; examples given by NCERT are Vallisneria, Hydrilla and the marine sea-grass Zostera. In most aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily the flowers emerge above the water and are pollinated by insects or wind, as in most land plants. Maize is wind-pollinated.
steps: Water hyacinth, water lily: insects or wind
solution.why_others_wrong: Water hyacinth and water lily are aquatic but their flowers are pollinated above the water by insects or wind; maize is a classic wind-pollinated plant.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination - agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option D: Hydrilla

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: As the anther matures, the microsporangia develop further and extend longitudinally all through the length of the anther, packed with pollen grains. These mature microsporangia are called:

options.text: Pollen sacs
Microspore tetrads
Sporogenous tissue
Germ pores

solution.explanation: NCERT: the microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains.
solution.why_others_wrong: Microspore tetrads are the four-celled products of meiosis; sporogenous tissue occupies the centre of a young microsporangium; germ pores are apertures in the pollen exine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', flower: stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain - the microsporangium
solution.final_answer: Option A: Pollen sacs

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Syngamy and triple fusion together make up double fertilisation. According to NCERT, double fertilisation is an event unique to:

options.text: Gymnosperms
Bryophytes
Flowering plants
Pteridophytes

solution.explanation: Since two types of fusion, syngamy and triple fusion, take place in an embryo sac, the phenomenon is termed double fertilisation, an event unique to flowering plants.
steps: Triple fusion: male gamete + two polar nuclei → PEN
solution.why_others_wrong: Gymnosperms, bryophytes and pteridophytes do not have triple fusion and so lack double fertilisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Flowering plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The early stages of embryo development, which are similar in both monocotyledons and dicotyledons, are referred to as:

options.text: Megasporogenesis
Embryogeny
Microsporogenesis
Apomixis

solution.explanation: The embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated. Though seeds differ greatly, the early stages of embryo development (embryogeny) are similar in both monocotyledons and dicotyledons.
steps: Early stages of embryo development = embryogeny
solution.why_others_wrong: Megasporogenesis and microsporogenesis form megaspores and microspores by meiosis; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events - embryo
solution.final_answer: Option B: Embryogeny

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a tender coconut, the coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm. The white kernel that surrounds it is:

options.text: Perisperm, a persistent part of the nucellus
The cotyledon of the embryo
The pericarp formed from the ovary wall
Cellular endosperm

solution.concept: Free-nuclear and cellular endosperm in coconut
solution.explanation: NCERT: the coconut water from tender coconut is free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei), and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm.
solution.why_others_wrong: Perisperm is residual nucellus (black pepper, beet); the cotyledon is part of the embryo; the pericarp is the fruit wall.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation: structures and events - endosperm
solution.final_answer: Option D: Cellular endosperm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In some species, the anther and stigma are placed at different positions, so that pollen cannot come in contact with the stigma of the same flower.
Statement II: Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT lists several devices that discourage self-pollination: non-synchrony of pollen release and stigma receptivity, placement of anther and stigma at different positions, self-incompatibility and unisexual flowers. Self-incompatibility is described as a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination - outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pistil and the ovule are correct?

(a) The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains.
(b) Inside the ovary is the ovarian cavity (locule).
(c) Each ovule has one or two protective envelopes called integuments.
(d) The placenta is located on the outer surface of the ovary wall.
(e) The embryo sac encloses the nucellus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Structure of the pistil and ovule
solution.explanation: The stigma is the landing platform for pollen; the style lies beneath it, and the basal bulged ovary encloses the ovarian cavity (locule). The placenta lies inside the ovarian cavity, and the ovules (megasporangia) arise from it. Each ovule has one or two integuments, which enclose the nucellus; the embryo sac (female gametophyte) lies within the nucellus.
steps: (d): false, the placenta is inside the ovarian cavity
(e): false, the nucellus encloses the embryo sac
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D each include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

Absolute alcohol

options.text: Light, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Darkness, carbon dioxide and a low temperature
Adequate moisture in the complete absence of oxygen
Adequate moisture, oxygen and suitable temperature

solution.explanation: As a seed matures, its water content falls and the embryo may become dormant. If favourable conditions are available (adequate moisture, oxygen and suitable temperature), the seed germinates.

options.text: The female flowers are emasculated and then bagged after they open
The female flower buds are bagged before the flowers open, without any emasculation
The female flowers are left unbagged, because they have no anthers
The female flowers are dusted with pollen while still in bud and then left open

solution.concept: Artificial hybridisation with unisexual female flowers
solution.explanation: Emasculation (removal of anthers) is needed only when the female parent has bisexual flowers. If the female parent bears unisexual flowers there is no need for emasculation; the female flower buds are bagged before the flowers open. When the stigma becomes receptive, pollination is done with the desired pollen and the flower is rebagged.
steps: Bag the female buds before opening
solution.why_others_wrong: Unisexual female flowers have no anthers to remove; leaving them unbagged risks contamination with unwanted pollen; pollination is done when the stigma is receptive, and the flower is rebagged.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination - artificial hybridisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: The female flower buds are bagged before the flowers open, without any emasculation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant of genotype Aa (female parent) is pollinated with pollen from a plant of genotype aa. Assuming normal megasporogenesis (monosporic development) and double fertilisation, which of the following correctly gives the possible genotypes of the seed coat, the embryo and the endosperm of the seeds formed?

options.text: Seed coat Aa; embryo Aa or aa; endosperm Aaa only
Seed coat aa; embryo Aa or aa; endosperm Aaa or aaa
Seed coat Aa; embryo AA or Aa; endosperm AAA or AAa
Seed coat Aa; embryo Aa or aa; endosperm AAa or aaa

solution.explanation: The seed coat develops from the integuments, which are maternal tissue (Aa). All nuclei of an embryo sac arise by mitosis from a single functional megaspore, which carries either A or a. So the egg and both polar nuclei carry the same allele. Male gametes carry a. Embryo = egg + male gamete: Aa or aa. Endosperm = two polar nuclei + male gamete: AA + a = AAa, or aa + a = aaa.
steps: Egg and polar nuclei from one megaspore: both A or both a
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Aaa only' wrongly assumes the two polar nuclei carry different alleles; option C gives the seed coat the pollen parent's genotype; option D forgets that the male gamete always carries a.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil and embryo sac; double fertilisation; seed
solution.final_answer: Option D: Seed coat Aa; embryo Aa or aa; endosperm AAa or aaa

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a typical angiosperm embryo sac, the egg cell and the two polar nuclei are genetically identical.
Reason (R): All the nuclei of the embryo sac are formed by mitotic divisions of the nucleus of a single functional megaspore.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Monosporic development of the embryo sac
solution.explanation: In most flowering plants only one of the four megaspores is functional. Its nucleus divides mitotically, and two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions give the 8-nucleate embryo sac. Mitosis produces genetically identical nuclei, so the egg and the polar nuclei (indeed all eight nuclei) carry the same genes. R is the direct cause of A.
steps: Mitosis from one nucleus → identical nuclei, so R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac: megasporogenesis and female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: An ovary has 30 ovules. Each ovule has a single megaspore mother cell, megasporogenesis is normal and monosporic, and every ovule forms a typical mature embryo sac. How many megaspores degenerate in all, and how many nuclei are present in all the mature embryo sacs together?

options.text: 120 megaspores degenerate; 240 nuclei
90 megaspores degenerate; 240 nuclei
90 megaspores degenerate; 210 nuclei
30 megaspores degenerate; 240 nuclei

solution.explanation: Each MMC undergoes meiosis to give four megaspores; in a majority of flowering plants one is functional and the other three degenerate. The functional megaspore forms an 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac.
solution.why_others_wrong: 120 counts all four megaspores as degenerating; 210 counts the 7 cells instead of the 8 nuclei; 30 assumes one degenerating megaspore per ovule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac: megasporogenesis and female gametophyte
solution.final_answer: Option B: 90 megaspores degenerate; 240 nuclei

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about pollinating agents are correct?

(a) Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds (sunbirds and humming birds) and bats are the common pollinating agents.
(b) Often, the flowers of an animal-pollinated species are specifically adapted for a particular species of animal.
(c) Pollination by wind is more common than pollination by water among abiotic pollinations.
(d) The majority of flowering plants use abiotic agents for pollination.
(e) Flowers pollinated by water are generally brightly coloured and rich in nectar.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a), (c), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: the majority of plants use biotic agents and only a small number use abiotic agents (wind, water); among abiotic pollinations, wind is more common. The listed animals are the common pollinating agents, and flowers of animal-pollinated species are often specifically adapted to a particular animal. Flowers pollinated by wind or water are not very colourful and do not produce nectar.
steps: (d): false, most plants use biotic agents
(e): false, water-pollinated flowers are not colourful and lack nectar
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D each include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination - agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Wind- and water-pollinated flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen compared with the number of ovules available for pollination.
Reason (R): In both wind and water pollination, the pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why abiotic pollination needs much pollen
solution.explanation: NCERT: pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination. To compensate for this uncertainty and the associated loss of pollen grains, the flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen compared with the number of ovules. R is the direct reason for A.
steps: Chance contact → pollen loss → enormous pollen production; R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollination - agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During double fertilisation, which cells of the embryo sac have their nucleus (or nuclei) fuse with a male gamete?

options.text: The egg cell and one synergid
The egg cell and the central cell
The two synergids
The central cell and the antipodal cells

solution.explanation: The pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of a synergid, but neither fuses with the synergid nucleus. One male gamete fuses with the egg nucleus (syngamy) to form the zygote; the other fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell (triple fusion) to form the primary endosperm nucleus. The synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilisation.
steps: Triple fusion: central cell (two polar nuclei)
Synergid only receives the gametes; antipodals degenerate
solution.why_others_wrong: The synergid receives the pollen tube contents but no fusion occurs with its nucleus; the antipodals take no part in fertilisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option B: The egg cell and the central cell

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Inheritance
B. Variation
C. Alleles
D. Heterozygous

List-II:
I. Slightly different forms of the same gene, coding for a pair of contrasting traits
II. Having two different alleles of a gene, as in Tt
III. Process by which characters are passed on from parent to progeny; the basis of heredity
IV. Degree by which progeny differ from their parents

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

solution.explanation: NCERT: inheritance is the process by which characters are passed on from parent to progeny and is the basis of heredity; variation is the degree by which progeny differ from their parents. Alleles are slightly different forms of the same gene that code for a pair of contrasting traits. TT and tt are homozygous, while Tt, which carries two different alleles, is heterozygous.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps inheritance and variation; option B swaps alleles and heterozygous; option C swaps inheritance and alleles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', introduction; inheritance of one gene
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Humans knew as early as 8000-1000 B.C. that one of the causes of variation was hidden in sexual reproduction, and they exploited the variations present in wild populations through artificial selection and domestication. The example NCERT gives of the result of such selection is:

options.text: Murrah buffaloes in Haryana
Hisardale sheep in Punjab
Sahiwal cows in Punjab
Jersey cattle in Gujarat

solution.explanation: NCERT: humans exploited variations in wild populations through artificial selection and domestication to create plants and animals with desired characters; for example, artificial selection and domestication from ancestral wild cows gave well-known Indian breeds such as Sahiwal cows in Punjab.
steps: Artificial selection and domestication of wild cows → Sahiwal cows of Punjab
solution.why_others_wrong: The other breeds are not the example NCERT uses in this chapter.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option C: Sahiwal cows in Punjab

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mendel proposed that something was being stably passed down, unchanged, from parent to offspring through the gametes over successive generations. He called these things:

options.text: Genes
Factors
Chromosomes
Alleles

solution.explanation: Mendel called the units being passed on 'factors'. Today we call them genes; genes are the units of inheritance that contain the information required to express a particular trait.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Genes' is the modern name, not Mendel's term; chromosomes and alleles were not part of Mendel's vocabulary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene
solution.final_answer: Option B: Factors

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cross between pea plants (T, tall, dominant over t, dwarf)) with List-II (fraction of progeny that are dwarf).

List-I:
A. Tt × tt
B. Tt × Tt
C. TT × tt
D. tt × tt

List-II:
I. 0
II. 1/4
III. 1
IV. 1/2

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

solution.explanation: Each parent passes one allele to each gamete. Tt × tt: gametes T, t × t → Tt : tt = 1 : 1, so 1/2 dwarf. Tt × Tt → TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so 1/4 dwarf. TT × tt → all Tt (tall), so 0 dwarf. tt × tt → all tt, so all (1) dwarf.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B swaps the test cross and the F1 self-cross; option C swaps TT × tt and tt × tt; option D swaps Tt × Tt and TT × tt.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A mutation arising due to a change in a single base pair of DNA is called a point mutation. A classical example of such a mutation is:

options.text: Down's syndrome
Turner's syndrome
Sickle-cell anaemia
Klinefelter's syndrome

solution.explanation: NCERT: mutation arising due to change in a single base pair of DNA is known as point mutation; a classical example is sickle-cell anaemia (GAG → GUG in the β-globin gene). Down's, Turner's and Klinefelter's syndromes involve the gain or loss of a whole chromosome (aneuploidy).
solution.why_others_wrong: The three syndromes are chromosomal disorders caused by aneuploidy, not by a single base change.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', mutation; genetic disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: Sickle-cell anaemia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In phenylketonuria, the affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into:

options.text: Phenylpyruvic acid
Tryptophan
Glutamic acid
Tyrosine

solution.explanation: Phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. The affected individual lacks the enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine. As a result phenylalanine accumulates and is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives, which accumulate in the brain and are excreted in urine.
solution.why_others_wrong: Phenylpyruvic acid is what phenylalanine is converted into because the normal conversion to tyrosine is blocked; tryptophan and glutamic acid are unrelated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders - phenylketonuria
solution.final_answer: Option D: Tyrosine

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Drosophila there is a clear differentiation of the sexes: the male and female flies are easily distinguishable.
Statement II: The hereditary variations of Drosophila can be seen only with an electron microscope.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the features that made Drosophila suitable for Morgan's genetic studies: it can be grown on a simple synthetic medium, completes its life cycle in about two weeks, a single mating gives a large number of progeny, there is a clear differentiation of the sexes (male and female flies are easily distinguishable) (Statement I true), and it has many types of hereditary variations that can be seen with low power microscopes, so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, the variations are visible with low power microscopes
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Genes A and B lie on the same chromosome, and the frequency of recombination between them is 20 per cent. A dihybrid that received AB from one parent and ab from the other is test-crossed with an aabb plant, and 1000 progeny are obtained. How many progeny of genotype Aabb are expected?

solution.explanation: The dihybrid forms parental gametes AB and ab and recombinant gametes Ab and aB. With 20 per cent recombination, recombinant gametes make up 20 per cent of the total, shared equally between Ab and aB (10 per cent each). In a test cross each gamete type appears directly as a progeny class, so Aabb = 10 per cent of 1000.
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 is the total of both recombinant classes; 400 is each parental class; 250 assumes independent assortment (1 : 1 : 1 : 1).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option B: 100

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A single pleiotropic gene can affect several different phenotypic traits.
Reason (R): In most cases, the gene exerts its effect on metabolic pathways that contribute towards different phenotypes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A pleiotropic gene is a single gene that can exhibit multiple phenotypic expressions. NCERT: the underlying mechanism of pleiotropy in most cases is the effect of a gene on metabolic pathways which contribute towards different phenotypes. R gives the cause of A.
steps: One gene → metabolic pathway → several phenotypes; R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: pleiotropy
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a family, both parents are affected by a trait controlled by a single autosomal gene, but one of their children is unaffected. The trait must be:

options.text: Recessive, with both parents heterozygous
Recessive, with one parent homozygous
Dominant, with both parents heterozygous
Dominant, with both parents homozygous

solution.concept: Dominant and recessive inheritance of a single autosomal gene
solution.explanation: If the trait were recessive, affected parents would both be homozygous recessive and every child would be affected. An unaffected child of two affected parents is possible only if the trait is dominant and each parent carries one recessive (normal) allele, i.e. both are heterozygous; then 1/4 of the children are expected to be unaffected.
solution.why_others_wrong: Affected individuals cannot be heterozygous for a recessive trait; two homozygous dominant parents cannot produce an unaffected (recessive homozygous) child.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: law of dominance and law of segregation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Dominant, with both parents heterozygous

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about mutation are correct?

(a) Besides recombination, mutation is another phenomenon that leads to variation in DNA.
(b) Many chemical and physical factors that induce mutations are referred to as mutagens.
(c) Mutation results in alteration of DNA sequences and consequently in changes in the genotype and the phenotype of an organism.
(d) Mutations occur only in genes located on the sex chromosomes.
(e) A change in the number of chromosomes cannot cause any disorder.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (c) and (d) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.concept: Mutation as a source of variation
solution.explanation: NCERT: mutation is a phenomenon that results in alteration of DNA sequences and consequently changes in the genotype and phenotype; besides recombination, it is another phenomenon that leads to variation in DNA. Many chemical and physical factors (e.g. UV radiation) induce mutations and are called mutagens. Mutations occur in autosomal as well as sex-linked genes, and changes in chromosome number cause disorders such as Down's syndrome.
steps: (d): false, autosomal genes also mutate (e.g. sickle-cell anaemia)
(e): false, aneuploidy causes Down's, Turner's and Klinefelter's syndromes
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C each include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', mutation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Sutton united the knowledge of chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles and called it the chromosomal theory of inheritance.
Statement II: Thomas Hunt Morgan and his colleagues worked with the tiny fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Sutton united the knowledge of chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles and called it the chromosomal theory of inheritance. Its experimental verification came from Thomas Hunt Morgan and his colleagues, who worked with the tiny fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A woman is red-green colour blind. Which of the following must be true of her parents?

options.text: Her mother must be colour blind
Her father must be colour blind
Her father may have normal vision if her mother is a carrier
Both her parents must be colour blind

solution.concept: Inheritance of an X-linked recessive trait
solution.explanation: Colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive disorder; a colour-blind woman has the recessive allele on both her X chromosomes. One X came from her father, who has only one X, so he must be colour blind. Her other X came from her mother, who must carry the allele but may be only a carrier (normal vision).
steps: Paternal X: Xᶜ → father XᶜY, colour blind
Maternal X: Xᶜ → mother at least a carrier
solution.why_others_wrong: The mother need only be a carrier, so neither A nor D must be true; a father with normal vision has a normal X and could not give his daughter Xᶜ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders - colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option B: Her father must be colour blind

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio of Mendel's dihybrid F2 can be derived as:

options.text: The sum of two monohybrid ratios, i.e. (3 : 1) + (3 : 1)
The product of two genotypic ratios, i.e. (1 : 2 : 1) × (1 : 2 : 1)
The product of two test-cross ratios, i.e. (1 : 1) × (1 : 1)
A combination series of 3 yellow : 1 green with 3 round : 1 wrinkled, i.e. (3 : 1) × (3 : 1)

solution.explanation: Because the two genes segregate independently, the dihybrid phenotypic ratio is the product of the two monohybrid phenotypic ratios: (3 Round : 1 Wrinkled)(3 Yellow : 1 Green) = 9 round yellow : 3 wrinkled yellow : 3 round green : 1 wrinkled green.
solution.why_others_wrong: Adding ratios has no meaning for combined traits; (1:2:1)² gives the 9 genotypic classes; (1:1)² is the dihybrid test-cross ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option D: A combination series of 3 yellow : 1 green with 3 round : 1 wrinkled, i.e. (3 : 1) × (3 : 1)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Henking gave the name 'X body' to the structure he observed during spermatogenesis, but he could not explain its significance.
Statement II: Henking himself identified the X body as a chromosome that determines maleness.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Henking (1891) traced a specific nuclear structure through spermatogenesis in a few insects, named it the X body and could not explain its significance (Statement I true). Further investigations by other scientists led to the conclusion that the X body was in fact a chromosome, which was named the X chromosome (Statement II false).
steps: Statement II: false, later workers showed it was a chromosome
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A pea plant with round yellow seeds is crossed with a plant with wrinkled green seeds (rryy). The progeny have round yellow and round green seeds in a 1 : 1 ratio. The genotype of the round yellow parent is:

options.text: RRYy
RrYy
RrYY
RRYY

solution.explanation: In a test cross, the progeny classes reflect the gametes of the tested parent. All progeny are round, so the parent gives only R gametes (RR). Yellow and green appear 1 : 1, so it is Yy. Hence RRYy, giving RY and Ry gametes in equal numbers.
solution.why_others_wrong: RrYy would give four classes (1 : 1 : 1 : 1); RrYY would give round yellow and wrinkled yellow; RRYY would give only round yellow.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: test cross; inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option A: RRYy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Individuals with Klinefelter's syndrome are sterile.
Reason (R): Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes, i.e. the karyotype 45 with X0.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome (47, XXY) gives an overall masculine development with some feminine features (gynaecomastia), and such individuals are sterile, so A is true. Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one X chromosome (45 with X0), so R is true. R describes a different disorder and does not explain why Klinefelter individuals are sterile.
steps: R concerns Turner's syndrome, not the sterility of Klinefelter males
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: With three alleles (Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i), the ABO gene gives six possible genotypes in the human population. Using the same reasoning, how many genotypes would be possible in a population for a gene with four alleles, and how many of these would be heterozygous?

options.text: 16 genotypes, of which 12 are heterozygous
10 genotypes, of which 4 are heterozygous
10 genotypes, of which 6 are heterozygous
8 genotypes, of which 4 are heterozygous

solution.explanation: A diploid individual carries only two alleles. With n alleles, the homozygotes number n and the heterozygotes number n(n − 1)/2, giving n(n + 1)/2 genotypes in all. For ABO, n = 3: 3 + 3 = 6. For n = 4: 4 homozygotes + 6 heterozygotes = 10.
solution.why_others_wrong: 16 counts ordered pairs (a1a2 and a2a1 separately); '4 heterozygous' confuses the homozygote count; 8 (2n) has no basis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance (multiple alleles in ABO blood groups)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 10 genotypes, of which 6 are heterozygous

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In honey bees, a queen of genotype Aa mates with a drone of genotype A. What genotypes are expected among their sons and their daughters?

options.text: Sons: AA or Aa (1 : 1); daughters: A or a (1 : 1)
Sons: all A, like their father; daughters: AA or Aa (1 : 1)
Sons: Aa only; daughters: AA, Aa and aa (1 : 2 : 1)
Sons: A or a (1 : 1); daughters: AA or Aa (1 : 1)

solution.explanation: An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg develops as a female, while an unfertilised egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis; males are haploid. Sons therefore carry only one maternal allele (A or a, 1 : 1) and have no father. Daughters get one allele from the egg (A or a) and the drone's A from the sperm: AA or Aa (1 : 1).
steps: Sons: unfertilised eggs → A or a
Daughters: egg (A/a) + sperm (A) → AA or Aa
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A reverses the sexes; sons have no father, so they cannot inherit the drone's allele (option B); the drone is haploid and gives only A, so no aa daughter is possible (option C).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in honey bee
solution.final_answer: Option D: Sons: A or a (1 : 1); daughters: AA or Aa (1 : 1)

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; mutations and genetic code

Which of the following statements about the methods of the Human Genome Project are correct?

(a) For sequencing, the total DNA from a cell was isolated and converted into random fragments of relatively smaller sizes.
(b) The sequences of the fragments were arranged on the basis of overlapping regions, using specialised computer-based programs.
(c) Genetic and physical maps were assigned using information on polymorphism of restriction endonuclease recognition sites and repetitive sequences known as microsatellites.
(d) The human DNA was sequenced as one intact molecule, without breaking it into fragments.
(e) Expressed sequence tags (ESTs) refers to sequencing the whole genome, coding and non-coding, and assigning functions to its regions later.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.concept: Methodology of the Human Genome Project
solution.explanation: NCERT: total DNA was converted into random small fragments, cloned in hosts using vectors and sequenced with automated sequencers. The sequences were arranged using overlapping regions, which needed specialised computer programs because alignment was humanly impossible. Genetic and physical maps were generated using polymorphism of restriction endonuclease recognition sites and microsatellites. ESTs focus on genes expressed as RNA; sequencing the whole genome and assigning functions later is sequence annotation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C each include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: methodologies

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A eukaryotic structural gene consists of exons E1, E2 and E3 separated by introns I1 and I2 (E1-I1-E2-I2-E3). After processing in the nucleus, the mRNA transported to the cytoplasm contains:

options.text: E1-E2-E3 joined in the same order, with a methyl guanosine triphosphate cap at the 5'-end and a poly-A tail at the 3'-end
E1-I1-E2-I2-E3, with a cap at the 5'-end and a poly-A tail at the 3'-end
I1-I2 joined together, with a cap and a tail
E1-E2-E3 joined in the same order, without any cap or tail

solution.explanation: The primary transcript (hnRNA) contains both exons and introns and is non-functional. It undergoes splicing, in which introns are removed and exons are joined in a defined order, and capping (methyl guanosine triphosphate added to the 5'-end) and tailing (200-300 adenylate residues added to the 3'-end). The fully processed hnRNA, now mRNA, is transported out of the nucleus for translation.
steps: Splicing: introns out, exons joined in order
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B is the unspliced primary transcript; introns are removed, not retained (option C); mature mRNA is capped and tailed (option D).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: processing in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option A: E1-E2-E3 joined in the same order, with a methyl guanosine triphosphate cap at the 5'-end and a poly-A tail at the 3'-end

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

steps: A: true (many codons → one amino acid)
R: true (one codon → one amino acid)
Different properties; R does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code

'Pro life', although the word means 'against life' in the context of disease-causing organisms
'Against life', because they are produced only by human cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following gives the correct sequence of steps in the treatment of municipal sewage?

options.text: Sedimentation → sequential filtration → settling tank → aeration tank → anaerobic sludge digester
Sequential filtration → sedimentation → anaerobic sludge digester → aeration tank → settling tank
Sequential filtration → aeration tank → sedimentation → anaerobic sludge digester → settling tank
Sequential filtration → sedimentation → aeration tank (flocs form) → settling tank (activated sludge) → anaerobic sludge digester

solution.explanation: Primary treatment removes floating debris by sequential filtration and grit by sedimentation, giving the primary effluent. In secondary treatment the effluent is aerated in large tanks where aerobic microbes form flocs and reduce the BOD; it is then passed to a settling tank where the flocs sediment as activated sludge. A small part of the sludge is pumped back as inoculum; the major part goes to anaerobic sludge digesters.
solution.why_others_wrong: Filtration precedes sedimentation; the aeration tank comes before the settling tank; the anaerobic digester receives activated sludge from the settling tank, so it comes last.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option D: Sequential filtration → sedimentation → aeration tank (flocs form) → settling tank (activated sludge) → anaerobic sludge digester

Of a given species living in a well-defined geographical area, sharing or competing for similar resources and potentially interbreeding

Endoparasites
Brood parasites
Commensals

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population grows according to the logistic model, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], in a habitat with carrying capacity K = 500. When N = 400, its actual growth rate is what percentage of the growth rate it would have had under exponential growth (dN/dt = rN) with the same r and the same N?

options.text: 80 per cent
25 per cent
20 per cent
0 per cent

solution.concept: Effect of the logistic factor (K − N)/K
solution.explanation: Dividing the logistic rate by the exponential rate gives (K − N)/K = (500 − 400)/500 = 0.2, i.e. 20 per cent. As N approaches K, this factor falls towards zero and the growth rate slows.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth - growth models
solution.final_answer: Option C: 20 per cent

questions.subject: Botany

The fitness of one species, measured in terms of its 'r' (intrinsic rate of increase), is significantly lower in the presence of another species
One species benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefited
One species lives on or in another and derives its nourishment from it

solution.explanation: NCERT defines competition as a process in which the fitness of one species (measured in terms of its 'r', intrinsic rate of increase) is significantly lower in the presence of another species. It can occur even between unrelated species and even when resources are not limiting (interference competition).
steps: Competition: lowered r of one species in the presence of another
solution.why_others_wrong: Mutual benefit is mutualism; one benefiting with the other unaffected is commensalism; living on or in a host for nourishment is parasitism.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: competition

questions.subject: Botany

Equal survival of all individuals irrespective of their fitness

Since the dependence on mimicry (R) is what makes pollination sensitive to the bee's appearance, R explains A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Consider the exponential model dN/dt = rN and the logistic model dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) When N is very small compared with K, logistic growth is nearly exponential.
(b) In logistic growth, dN/dt is maximum when N = K.
(c) In logistic growth, the per capita growth rate decreases as N increases.
(d) In exponential growth, the per capita growth rate remains constant at r.
(e) In exponential growth, dN/dt does not depend on N.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (c) and (d) only
(c), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: Per capita rate = (dN/dt)/N. Exponential: (dN/dt)/N = r, a constant, while dN/dt = rN rises with N. Logistic: per capita rate = r(K − N)/K, which falls as N rises; when N ≪ K the factor (K − N)/K ≈ 1 and growth is nearly exponential. When N = K the factor is zero, so dN/dt = 0 (the asymptote), not maximum.
steps: (e): dN/dt = rN depends on N → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A includes (b), option B includes (b) and (e), and option D includes (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', populations: population growth - growth models

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population of 2000 individuals has a per capita birth rate of 0.1 and a per capita death rate of 0.04 per individual per year. During the year, 30 individuals immigrate and 50 emigrate. Using N(t+1) = N(t) + [(B + I) − (D + E)], the population after one year is:
